title: Form Facet
description: Accreted binding facet for form/template source, sibling to the procedure facet. Single-writer: the headwater authoring agent (form-specialized). Models a form TEMPLATE (a blank instrument) — never a submission. A filled-in form is an instance with real data (potential PII); it is a record/learner-model object under separate governance and is NOT modeled here. The action/label text lives in meaning.source_text; structure (sections, order) lives in the object facet; provenance lives in governance. This facet holds only what is irreducibly about capturing structured input. field_type and content_disposition are MIRRORS of vocab/form.enum.json (vocab wins; a conformance check asserts schema enum == vocab ids). performed_by reuses roles.registry and captures_record reuses records.registry — the SAME registries the procedure facet uses; no form-specific copy. v0.2 adds constraints.slots: NAMED fill-in points inside otherwise-retained text, so an instance overlay can key on (atom_id, slot_id) instead of a position in a string. v0.3 adds slots[].marker — the exact bracketed literal the slot stands for — because naming the slots was necessary but not sufficient: without a marker a renderer must still match spans to ids BY POSITION, which is the very thing v0.2 set out to eliminate. v0.4 adds evidence_kind and supplied_by, at BOTH the field and the slot level: a template's unfilled points enumerate a demand on someone outside the manifold, and naming that demand in governed terms is what makes tools/project_socket.py able to derive an intake contract instead of a checklist. MIRRORS of vocab/evidence.enum.json. v0.5 tracks evidence.v0.2 (determination, structured_set) — a mirror bump, no shape change.

field_type.description: Governed input primitive. Present on form_field leaves; omitted on form/form_section containers. MIRROR of vocab/form.enum.json field_type ids.

content_disposition.description: Authoring lifecycle of this field's standard/source text, from the form template's own rules. MIRROR of vocab/form.enum.json content_disposition ids.

evidence_kind.description: What kind of evidence this demand requires. Present on a DEMAND — an authorable field, or a field whose slots leave points unfilled. Omitted elsewhere: a controlled_standard sentence with no slots demands nothing, and an instructional_transient block is deleted rather than filled. MIRROR of vocab/evidence.enum.json evidence_kind ids. Deliberately NOT derived from field_type — text_short covers both an identifier and a version stamp — so this is a recorded judgment read off the demand's own expects/source text, with the same standing as content_disposition read off the template's colour convention.

supplied_by.description: Who the demand falls on: the stakeholder's asset evidence, the operator's authoring context, or a named body's decision. MIRROR of vocab/evidence.enum.json supplied_by ids. Keeps the intake contract honest — a version number is not part of gathering an evidence dossier. Present wherever evidence_kind is.

constraints.description: Validation/integrity rules on the accepted value. Embedded (they ARE part of the field's invariant truth), not a reference.

slots.description: Named fill-in points inside this field's source_text — the [bracketed] spans a template leaves for the author inside text that is otherwise retained unchanged. A field like this has genuinely MIXED disposition: the sentence is controlled_standard, the slots are authorable. The facet carries one disposition per field, so the slots are declared here instead. NAMED, never positional: an instance overlay keys on (atom_id, slot_id), and a positional reference ('slot 2') would shift the moment anyone edits the sentence — exactly what stable ids exist to prevent. Each slot names its own marker — the literal bracketed span it fills — so the mapping survives an edit to the surrounding sentence. No field_type here on purpose: repeating that closed list would spawn a drifting second copy.

id.description: Stable name, unique within this field. Half of the (atom_id, slot_id) key.

expects.description: What the author must supply here, in plain words.

evidence_kind.description: As the field-level property, for this slot. A slot is a demand in its own right — the (atom_id, slot_id) key IS the demand id in the intake socket — so it carries its own kind rather than inheriting the sentence's.

supplied_by.description: As the field-level property, for this slot.

options_ref.description: Controlled value set, when the slot takes one. A pattern, not an enum — no closed list is copied here.

marker.description: The exact [bracketed] literal in the field's source_text that this slot stands for, e.g. '[ASPXXXX]'. Substitution is then a literal match on the marker, never an index into a list of spans — so re-ordering or rewording the sentence around a marker cannot silently re-point a filled value at the wrong blank. Must occur EXACTLY ONCE in source_text; the gate checks it. If the marker text itself is edited, meaning changed, content_hash moves, and every instance value on this field is correctly reported stale.

options_ref.description: Registry id of the controlled value set for select_one/select_many. Reference the option set; never embed it.

captures_record.description: records.registry id (rec_...) this field/form populates — the GxP evidence link. SAME registry as procedure.produces_records.

performed_by.description: roles.registry ids (role_...) accountable to complete/sign this field. Roles, never people (no PII). SAME registry as procedure.performed_by.

conditional_on.description: Show/require logic: this field applies only when the referenced field-atom holds the given value. Mirrors procedure.branches at the field level.
